slot.brief: Cylindrical vessel full of liquid rotated at angular speed ω; find height difference between edge and centre or pressure at a point using parabolic free-surface relation.

stem: Water of initial depth $0.50$ m in a cylindrical vessel of radius $0.40$ m is brought to steady rotation at $5$ rad s$^{-1}$. If no water spills, what is the gauge pressure at the bottom centre? Take $\rho=1000$ kg m$^{-3}$ and $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$.

verdicts.working: For rigid rotation, the free surface is z(r)=z_c+ω²r²/(2g). Volume conservation gives z_c=h₀−ω²R²/(4g)=0.50−0.10=0.40 m. Bottom-centre gauge pressure is ρgz_c=1000×10×0.40=4.0×10³ Pa.

working:
$h(r)=h_c+\dfrac{\omega^2r^2}{2g}$. Volume conservation gives $h_0=h_c+\dfrac{\omega^2R^2}{4g}$, so $h_c=0.50-\dfrac{25(0.40)^2}{40}=0.40$ m. $p_g=\rho gh_c=1000(10)(0.40)=4.0\times10^3$ Pa.

Independent check: For rigid rotation, the free surface is z(r)=z_c+ω²r²/(2g). Volume conservation gives z_c=h₀−ω²R²/(4g)=0.50−0.10=0.40 m. Bottom-centre gauge pressure is ρgz_c=1000×10×0.40=4.0×10³ Pa.
solution:
For rigid rotation, the free-surface height is $h(r)=h_c+\dfrac{\omega^2r^2}{2g}$. Volume conservation gives
$$h_c=h_0-\frac{\omega^2R^2}{4g}=0.50-\frac{25(0.40)^2}{40}=0.40\ \text{m}.$$
Thus, the bottom-centre gauge pressure is $p_g=\rho gh_c=1000(10)(0.40)=4.0\times10^3\ \text{Pa}$. ⊳
